text:
**Findings**
High: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:70) lines 70-81 lets any same-rank terminal state overwrite an existing terminal record, so an older `FAILED`/`CANCELLED` row can replace a newer `COMPLETED` row with later `end`/`elapsed_sec`.

High: [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:110) lines 110-114 and 148-151 accept negative GPU and CPU counts, which can produce negative CPU/GPU-hour reports instead of rejecting malformed accounting data.

Medium: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:74) lines 74-80 marks a row unchanged based only on `state`, `end`, and `elapsed_sec`, dropping corrected `alloc_cpus`, `gpus`, `user`, `partition`, or `exit_code` values.

Medium: [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:14) lines 14, 65, 83, 101, and 115 compare ISO timestamps as raw strings; mixed naive and timezone-offset datetimes are misfiltered. I reproduced an equal instant being excluded when `--since` includes `+00:00`.

Medium: [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:154) lines 154-155 stores empty `User` and `Partition` values without validation, creating blank report groups despite the DB declaring those columns `NOT NULL`.

Medium: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13) lines 13-26 plus [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:58) lines 58-70, 79-106, and 135-148 define no indexes for reference-time or grouping queries; every report is a full table scan and uses temp B-trees as data grows.

Low: [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:121) lines 121-126, 138-143, and 176-180 do not handle SQLite/opening errors, so unreadable paths, corrupt databases, or permission failures surface as tracebacks instead of actionable CLI errors.

**Score**
6.5/10. The code is small, readable, parameterized against SQL injection, and has a meaningful test suite. I would not call it production-ready because the accounting merge rules and timestamp semantics can silently corrupt or misreport results.

**Rewrite Estimate**
About 140 lines need rewriting or significant change: stricter parsing/validation, timestamp normalization/storage, upsert conflict rules, schema/index changes, CLI error handling, and focused tests for those cases.

**PR Decision**
No, I would not approve this as-is. The current defects are fixable, but silent accounting inaccuracies are too risky for a usage-reporting tool.

Verification: `python -m pytest -q` passed with 61 tests. `compileall` could not write `__pycache__` because `/work` is read-only in this environment.

issues.description: Same-rank terminal states can overwrite newer terminal records with stale state, end time, and elapsed values.
Negative GPU and CPU counts are accepted, allowing negative usage totals.
Unchanged detection ignores corrected user, partition, CPU, GPU, and exit-code fields.
Timestamp filtering uses lexicographic string comparison, which misbehaves with timezone-offset datetimes.
Empty user and partition fields are accepted and later appear as blank report groups.
Schema has no indexes for report reference-time or grouping queries, forcing full scans as the database grows.
SQLite connection/query failures are uncaught and surface as tracebacks instead of clean CLI errors.
